title: Manny's Tavern on Bourbon Street
summary: They played weekends in the back dance hall at Manny's, where tourists and young players like Pete Fountain sat in.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Let me ask you about some of the earlier episodes again. Do you remember playing at Manny's? Manny's Tavern.

Manny's Tavern. Benefit and Sing Rock. Tell me about that. Yeah, well we played back there every weekend. On Friday nights, Saturday nights, no Sundays. We played back there every weekend. Oh, I can't say how long we played back there. We stayed there for quite a while before we went on Boyfriend Street. See, that was when we first went back there, it was Manny's.
What sort of a place was it?
Nice place. Very nice. Never had no trouble back there at all. Dancing?

Because we was playing back in the dance hall. You see, the bar was up in the front. And the dance hall was in the back. Big dance hall. So there was a lot of tourists that used to come back there, you know, and listen to us. Pete Fountain used to come there before he started. And Frank Asunder and his brother, Freddie, they used to come and sit in with us. And this young trumpet player there, George, I can't think of his last name. But he was a wonderful trumpet man. He used to play with the bass of Street Six. He was playing that, what you call it, that, Fuebren and Conti. Well, he used to work that one time every night until he died.
Yes, I know he was a trumpet player.
Yeah, his name was George. He was an Italian fellow, too. Well, yeah, we played at Manley's a long time before we got to a real break.
